title: chunkbackoff-repro-cheatsheet
content:
Purpose: quick, reproducible notes for a flaky streaming issue where clients intermittently get truncated JSON events or long pauses during SSE/chunked responses. Keep this as a playbook I can run locally and hand off to SRE.

Summary of symptom:
- Clients see 5–20s stalls mid-response followed by a burst of several chunks.
- Occasionally the stream ends with a partial JSON object (truncated last line).
- More common under bursty traffic or when client concurrency is > 10.

Context / recent changes:
- Runtime: inference-gpu-rt v2.14 deployed Feb 2026 (KV cache changes + adaptive write batching).
- Proxy: nginx 1.24 with upstream keepalive pool.
- Observed after enabling dynamic batch coalescing experiment.

Minimal repro (local):
1) Start a toy server that mimics runtime behavior (node/python). I use the python example below to emulate periodic flushes + random pause.

python repro_server.py (content below)
# repro_server.py (quick)
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
import time, json, random

class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header('Content-type','text/event-stream')
        self.send_header('Cache-Control','no-cache')
        self.end_headers()
        for i in range(1,21):
            # simulate chunk assembly + occasional long pause
            payload = json.dumps({\"i\": i, \"partial\": False}) + '\\n'
            self.wfile.write(b'data: ' + payload.encode('utf-8'))
            self.wfile.write(b\"\\n\\n\")
            self.wfile.flush()
            # random long pause mimics backpressure/backoff
            if random.random() < 0.12:
                time.sleep(6 + random.random()*4)
            else:
                time.sleep(0.2)

httpd = HTTPServer(('0.0.0.0', 8083), H)
print('repro server ready')
httpd.serve_forever()

2) From client side test with different clients to see behavior differences:
- curl (no buffer): curl -v --no-buffer "http://localhost:8083/"
- httpie: http --stream GET http://localhost:8083/
- python requests streaming:
  import requests
  r = requests.get('http://localhost:8083/', stream=True)
  for chunk in r.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True):
      print('LINE:', chunk)
- node EventSource (eventsource polyfill) or fetch with ReadableStream for chunk boundaries.

Observed differences locally:
- curl prints immediately but when server sleeps > 5s, curl sometimes shows buffered sections then all data suddenly appears as a block (not always incremental).
- requests.iter_lines yields partial lines if "+\\n\\n" not flushed exactly (requests tolerates).
- Browser EventSource tends to preserve ordering but the UI may appear "stuck" until a buffer threshold is hit.

Commands I ran against the real environment:
- curl -v --no-buffer "https://api.redwood-inference/examples/stream?model=gptx&max_tokens=256" 2>&1 | tee /tmp/stream-curl.log
- sudo tcpdump -A -s0 port 443 and filter by client IP to capture raw chunk boundaries (pcap)
- ngrep -W byline host api.redwood-inference and inspect CRLF patterns

Log snippets from runtime (sanitized):
[2026-03-03T14:11:22.327Z] INFO write_loop: wrote 1024 bytes to conn_id=xyz
[2026-03-03T14:11:22.328Z] DEBUG flush_policy: batch_timer_ms=50, queued_tokens=34, coalesced=false
[2026-03-03T14:11:28.961Z] WARN write_loop: write stalled for 6.5s (client_recv_window small?), conn_id=xyz
[2026-03-03T14:11:29.005Z] INFO resume write_loop: wrote 8192 bytes after stall
[2026-03-03T14:11:29.006Z] ERROR client: incomplete send, truncated_output=true, conn_id=xyz

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Adaptive coalescing introduces long timers for small windows. If a client or proxy imposes backpressure, the runtime marks write as stalled and then flushes large coalesced chunks — causing client buffering and occasional truncation when connection closes during flush.
2) Nginx proxy buffering (proxy_buffering on) combined with chunked SSE may re-chunk at upstream boundaries; if upstream closes mid-flush, proxy sends a last partial chunk.
3) TLS record layering + TCP_NODELAY interactions: the runtime flushes several small writes that the kernel then bundles; some clients/OSes wait for certain flush patterns before exposing to app.
4) Client-side EventSource polyfills occasionally reassemble on message boundaries; if message doesn't end with final "\\n\\n" block (two newlines for SSE), the client keeps waiting. A partial write can leave left-over carriage returns.

Quick checks to validate hypotheses:
- Disable runtime coalescing (set env ADAPTIVE_COALESCE=0) and run load test. If stalls disappear, suspect hypothesis #1.
- On a reproducer, toggle nginx proxy_buffering off: proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; and test.
- Use socat to connect to runtime and capture raw TCP frames (bypass proxy) to check chunk boundaries.

Replication commands I keep using: (these are copy/paste friendly)
1) Raw TCP capture (requires root): sudo tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/stream.pcap tcp and then filter in Wireshark for TLS record boundaries.
2) ngrep to show plaintext SSE (for non-TLS test): ngrep -q -W byline "^data:" tcp and host 127.0.0.1 and port 8083
3) Simple load tester (hey or wrk) to trigger backpressure: wrk -t12 -c100 -d30s "http://localhost:8083/"

Edgecases noticed while iterating:
- When client count is low but concurrency spikes sporadically, the runtime switches from small flushes to a large coalesced write which triggers buffering in Nginx.
- In some runs, a single client sees two partial JSON objects at the end; code-path on connection close tries to write a trailing partial, raises truncated_output flag.

Recent timeline & next steps (personal TODO):
- [Done] Repro locally with python server; verified curl buffering behavior.
- [Done] Capture runtime logs showing "write stalled" entries.
- [Next] Spin a canary without adaptive coalesce (env toggle) and run synthetic load for 1 hour.
- [Next] Recreate with real nginx in front of runtime on staging and toggle proxy_buffering.
- [Next] Add unit test for flush() semantics in the runtime write path to ensure partial writes are retried and not left as truncated flag when connection actively closes during flush.

Notes-to-self when handing off:
- Include tcpdump pcap and runtime debug log (write_loop traces).
- Mark sample client IPs and exact request IDs.
- If SRE asks about "truncated_output" flag, point them to write_loop and the backpressure metric (write_stall_ms).

Misc experiments that failed / false leads:
- Turning on TCP_CORK on the runtime socket reduced number of writes but made stalls worse (not a fix).
- Increasing Nginx proxy_buffers to a very large value hid symptoms but didn't fix truncation when connection closes abruptly.

References and related tickets:
- INC-4522: "SSE clients get partial JSON on high burst traffic" (initial incident report)
- GH-1398: PR that added adaptive coalescing (author: @ravi)

If you pick this up: start by running the ADAPTIVE_COALESCE toggle locally, then reproduce with wrk + nginx proxy. If you get stuck, ask Ravi for a quick walkthrough of the coalescing state machine (he added detailed logs).

Timestamped scratch entries (for my memory):
- 2026-02-10 09:34 - first noticed in staging during nightly load test.
- 2026-02-14 11:02 - confirmed logs contain "write stalled" at same times as client stalls.
- 2026-03-03 14:20 - reproduced locally with python server that sleeps mid-stream.

End of sheet. Keep this short, run commands, paste logs into ticket when escalating.
